opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Jennifer Martin (E033) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E033 (Jennifer Martin) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors max out at read without advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Jennifer Martin (E033) requested admin access to Payroll. Per the Security note, the DB shows E033 is a contractor with basic security training, so the maximum allowed access is read (contractors with basic training get read; contractors never get admin). Even under the full-time interpretation in the earlier note, an Analyst would max at write since Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. The requested admin exceeds the maximum in all cases, so I grant the maximum of read, and no more than requested.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jennifer Martin (E033)
Requested: admin access to Payroll

Notes:
Note 1 (from HR?): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write
Note 2 (from Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training: basic, recommendation for Payroll: read

There's a conflict between the two notes: one says full-time, other says contractor. The security note says the DB shows contractor, and note 1 was "previously noted" as full-time. The security note appears to be correcting the record.

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write, admin only if role owns system (Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist; Analyst doesn't own Payroll)
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic training: max read.
If full-time Analyst: max write (not admin since Analyst doesn't own Payroll).

Either way, requested admin exceeds maximum. The maximum is either read (contractor, basic training) or write (full-time Analyst). Given conflicting info, which to use?

The Security note seems to be the corrected record, with the most recent/authoritative info: contractor with basic security training. So maximum = read.

Never grant more than requested. Requested admin. Grant maximum = read.

So decision: read.

Evidence: E033 is a contractor with basic security training per security DB (Security note, ticket 1), so max is read; admin requested exceeds max, so grant read. Even under the full-time interpretation, max would be write (Analyst doesn't own Payroll), so admin would still be denied. But grant read per contractor status.

I'll submit read.
